blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 2.5
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 2.5

blocks.text: विद्यासमुत्थाने स्वाभाविके खेचरी शिवावस्था
blocks.directed: [slowly] विद्यासमुत्थाने स्वाभाविके खेचरी शिवावस्था

blocks.text: Vidyāsamutthāne svābhāvike khecarī śivāvasthā.
blocks.directed: Vidyāsamutthāne svābhāvike khecarī śivāvasthā.

blocks.text: When supreme knowledge arises spontaneously, Khecarī manifests as the state of Śiva.
blocks.directed: When supreme knowledge arises spontaneously, Khecarī manifests as the state of Śiva.

blocks.text: No, Khecarī Doesn’t Mean Shoving Your Tongue Up Your Nose.
blocks.directed: No, Khecarī Doesn’t Mean Shoving Your Tongue Up Your Nose.

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Right.

blocks.text: We’ve reached Khecarī.
blocks.directed: We’ve reached Khecarī.

blocks.text: And unfortunately, we’ve got to clear something up immediately.
blocks.directed: And unfortunately, we’ve got to clear something up immediately.

blocks.text: Because if you search for Khecarī Mudrā, you’re likely to encounter extremely flexible yogis doing extraordinary things with their tongues.
blocks.directed: Because if you search for Khecarī Mudrā, you’re likely to encounter extremely flexible yogis doing extraordinary things with their tongues.

blocks.text: In certain haṭhayoga traditions, khecarīmudrā refers to a technique involving the tongue and the upper palate.
blocks.directed: In certain haṭhayoga traditions, khecarīmudrā refers to a technique involving the tongue and the upper palate.

blocks.text: But that is not what Kṣemarāja means here.
blocks.directed: But that is not what Kṣemarāja means here.

blocks.text: And he explicitly distinguishes this sūtra’s Khecarī from physical or specialised yogic procedures promising extraordinary powers, including flight.
blocks.directed: And he explicitly distinguishes this sūtra’s Khecarī from physical or specialised yogic procedures promising extraordinary powers, including flight.

blocks.text: Quite.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Quite.

blocks.text: It’s always a relief when a medieval tantric philosopher tells you that you don’t have to rearrange your mouth to attain supreme consciousness.
blocks.directed: It’s always a relief when a medieval tantric philosopher tells you that you don’t have to rearrange your mouth to attain supreme consciousness.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Vidyā — knowledge, here supreme knowledge.
blocks.directed: Vidyā — knowledge, here supreme knowledge.

blocks.text: Samutthāna — arising, emergence.
blocks.directed: Samutthāna — arising, emergence.

blocks.text: Svābhāvika — natural, spontaneous, belonging to one’s own nature.
blocks.directed: Svābhāvika — natural, spontaneous, belonging to one’s own nature.

blocks.text: Khecarī — she who moves through kha, space or the sky.
blocks.directed: Khecarī — she who moves through kha, space or the sky.

blocks.text: Śivāvasthā — the state of Śiva.
blocks.directed: Śivāvasthā — the state of Śiva.

blocks.text: Now the word kha is doing something extremely important.
blocks.directed: Now the word kha is doing something extremely important.

blocks.text: In ordinary Sanskrit, it can mean space or sky.
blocks.directed: In ordinary Sanskrit, it can mean space or sky.

blocks.text: But in this tantric context, Kṣemarāja interprets it as the boundless space of consciousness.
blocks.directed: But in this tantric context, Kṣemarāja interprets it as the boundless space of consciousness.

blocks.text: So Khecarī is the power moving freely within that space.
blocks.directed: So Khecarī is the power moving freely within that space.

blocks.text: And when supreme knowledge arises naturally, the yogi enters the state of Śiva.
blocks.directed: And when supreme knowledge arises naturally, the yogi enters the state of Śiva.

blocks.text: Not the state of an individual who has acquired another special experience.
blocks.directed: Not the state of an individual who has acquired another special experience.

blocks.text: The state of recognising the nature of consciousness itself.
blocks.directed: The state of recognising the nature of consciousness itself.

blocks.text: Imagine the mind as a bird.
blocks.directed: Imagine the mind as a bird.

blocks.text: Ordinarily, it flies towards objects.
blocks.directed: Ordinarily, it flies towards objects.

blocks.text: A sound.
blocks.directed: A sound.

blocks.text: A memory.
blocks.directed: A memory.

blocks.text: A desire.
blocks.directed: A desire.

blocks.text: A fear.
blocks.directed: A fear.

blocks.text: It moves between limited things.
blocks.directed: It moves between limited things.

blocks.text: And its sense of freedom is conditioned by those things.
blocks.directed: And its sense of freedom is conditioned by those things.

blocks.text: But now the bird discovers something astonishing.
blocks.directed: But now the bird discovers something astonishing.

blocks.text: Its real freedom does not consist merely in choosing which object to fly towards.
blocks.directed: Its real freedom does not consist merely in choosing which object to fly towards.

blocks.text: The openness through which every movement is possible was never absent.
blocks.directed: The openness through which every movement is possible was never absent.

blocks.text: This is the metaphorical significance of Khecarī.
blocks.directed: This is the metaphorical significance of Khecarī.

blocks.text: Not a bird imprisoned in a box getting a slightly larger box.
blocks.directed: Not a bird imprisoned in a box getting a slightly larger box.

blocks.text: Not even a bird acquiring a particularly impressive pair of wings.
blocks.directed: Not even a bird acquiring a particularly impressive pair of wings.

blocks.text: But the recognition of the boundless conscious space in which its movements arise.
blocks.directed: But the recognition of the boundless conscious space in which its movements arise.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja links this with the spontaneous emergence of bliss.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja links this with the spontaneous emergence of bliss.

blocks.text: Ānanda.
blocks.directed: Ānanda.

blocks.text: Not simply ordinary pleasure.
blocks.directed: Not simply ordinary pleasure.

blocks.text: Not an exciting sensation that eventually disappears and leaves you wanting another one.
blocks.directed: Not an exciting sensation that eventually disappears and leaves you wanting another one.

blocks.text: But the delight associated with consciousness recognising its own freedom.
blocks.directed: But the delight associated with consciousness recognising its own freedom.

blocks.text: And notice what happened between 2.4 and 2.5.
blocks.directed: And notice what happened between 2.4 and 2.5.

blocks.text: At 2.4, the practitioner became fascinated by exceptional phenomena appearing within Māyā.
blocks.directed: At 2.4, the practitioner became fascinated by exceptional phenomena appearing within Māyā.

blocks.text: At 2.5, those limited accomplishments are subordinated to the spontaneous arising of supreme knowledge.
blocks.directed: At 2.5, those limited accomplishments are subordinated to the spontaneous arising of supreme knowledge.

blocks.text: It’s a complete reorientation.
blocks.directed: It’s a complete reorientation.

blocks.text: Instead of asking:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Instead of asking:

blocks.text: “What amazing thing can I experience next?”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “What amazing thing can I experience next?”

blocks.text: The yogi discovers the ground of experience itself.
blocks.directed: The yogi discovers the ground of experience itself.

blocks.text: And that, within Kṣemarāja’s interpretation, is the state of Śiva.
blocks.directed: And that, within Kṣemarāja’s interpretation, is the state of Śiva.

blocks.text: Not supernatural tourism.
blocks.directed: Not supernatural tourism.

blocks.text: Not a spiritual upgrade package.
blocks.directed: Not a spiritual upgrade package.

blocks.text: Recognition of the freedom that makes every experience possible.
blocks.directed: Recognition of the freedom that makes every experience possible.

blocks.text: Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
